Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for low-latency reranking and real-time chat across trading support products. Primary ask: firm throughput guarantees (tokens/sec), P99 latency SLOs <= 120ms for short-chat flows, predictable monthly committed GPU planning, flexible warm-pool sizing and clear SLA chargebacks for burst.

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria (customer language & notes):
- Throughput guarantees: sustained 40k tokens/sec for reranking cluster during market hours; 3x burst for 10min windows.
- Latency targets: p50 <= 30ms (short prompts), p95 <= 65ms, p99 <= 120ms for critical flows. Must include network egress times to their VPC.
- Reserved GPU planning: want committed pool (N=24 A100-equivalent GPUs) with ability to reserve + burst to shared capacity. Need explicit warm-pool sizing guidance (target warm pool = 20% of committed by default).
- Autoscaling policy expectations: scale-up fast (<90s warm-up), scale-down conservative (cooldown 10-15min) to avoid thrash during market microbursts. Prefer queue-length-based admission control rather than purely CPU/GPU utilization.
- Warm pools: pre-initialized model loads, maintain KV cache priming for top-20 prompt prefixes. Need billing transparency for pre-warmed nodes.
- Queueing & backpressure: prefer request queue threshold at 500 concurrent requests per pod, then route to degraded model variant (lower token cost) before rejecting. Graceful degradation plan required.
- Metrics: token/sec, GPU util distribution, batching efficiency, continous latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), cold-start counts.

POC plan / success metrics:
- 72-hr throughput run in their NA region against synthetic and replay traffic (we will supply the replay harness).
- Validate warm-pool effectiveness: measure cold-start reduction >= 90% compared to baseline.
- Autoscaling stress test: simulate market open microburst to validate scale-up time <= 90s and p99 <= targeted SLO when burst capacity used.
- Cost model: Redwood to provide per-GPU committed + burst pricing, warm-pool hourly rate, and billing examples for a 30-day heavy-usage month.

Commercial / SLA negotiation notes:
- AegisQuant pushing for credit for SLA breaches (monthly uptime + latency SLOs). They want penalties tiered and visible in contract.
- Ask to include explicit fallback routing guarantees (if dedicated pool saturated, route to private/hosted equivalent within same region with <= 200ms added latency).
- They also want a signed data-residency appendix + SOC2 Type II evidence and KMS integration clauses.

Open questions / engineering risks:
- How to measure and guarantee p99 across customer network path vs Redwood runtime? Need joint measurement spec.
- Warm-pool memory footprint for large models impacts how many VMs can be pre-warmed — ask infra for exact RAM/VRAM numbers per model variant.
- Admission control: need shared design for queueing thresholds + per-route priority (trading-critical vs analytics).
